CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

scooter is an R package (roxygen2 + testthat, not on CRAN) providing a data-agnostic framework for loading, preprocessing, and plotting single-cell RNA-seq datasets on top of Seurat.

Function-level behavior lives in roxygen, not here. Every exported function’s own @details/ @param/@return already explains its rationale, defaults, and what it writes — read the function (or man/<fn>.Rd) first. This file covers what roxygen can’t: cross-cutting conventions, the CLI script (inst/extdata/scrna-scooter.R, a docopt script with no roxygen of its own), and historical/deferred notes that don’t belong in documentation of current behavior.

Writing style

Write all prose for this project in Simplified Technical English (STE, per ASD-STE100). This applies to CLAUDE.md itself, roxygen comments (@param/@details/@return), inline # code comments, and chat responses while working in this repo.

  • Write one short sentence per instruction or fact. Keep sentences under 20 words.
  • Use active voice. Write “the function reads the file,” not “the file is read by the function.”
  • Use simple verb tenses. Prefer simple present. Avoid compound or complex tenses.
  • Use one term for one thing. Do not switch between synonyms for the same concept.
  • Avoid long noun strings. Write “the pattern to access the assay data layer,” not “the assay data layer access pattern.”
  • Prefer plain, common words over technical synonyms when a plain word means the same thing.
  • Technical names are exempt from the vocabulary rule above. Function names, package names, and R/Seurat/genomics terms (GetAssayData(), layer, assay, DimReduc, …) stay as they are — the sentence-structure rules above still apply around them.
  • Inline # code comments stay to one line. Use more than one line only when the code’s behavior is not obvious without it. This rule covers inline comments only, not roxygen (#') or file headers.
  • When you edit this file, skip rename history. Skip facts that the referenced file shows at once.

Environment (read this first)

The package targets Seurat v5. The code uses the layer= argument of GetAssayData()/SetAssayData(), which SeuratObject 4 does not have. The Seurat >= 5.3.1 floor comes from leiden_method = "igraph" in calculate_clusters(); everything else only needs 5.0.0.

Whatever R/Rscript is first on PATH needs to satisfy the Seurat/SeuratObject versions in DESCRIPTION and have the dev toolchain installed (devtools, roxygen2, testthat, pkgload). Check with Rscript -e 'packageVersion("Seurat")' if unsure. Then everything below runs with a plain Rscript call; no env activation step is needed.

scooter-package.R‘s @import dplyr/@import Seurat tags mean those packages’ functions resolve everywhere without per-function @importFrom tags — don’t add them elsewhere. DESCRIPTION sets Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) — without it, [fn()] cross-references render as dead literal bracket text, and a bare %/{/} in doc prose corrupts Rd parsing. Keep markdown mode on.

Seurat 5 conventions used here

  • Never touch assay slots directly. Assay5 has no @counts / @data / @scale.data; it holds a named layer list. Read with GetAssayData(obj, assay=, layer=), write with SetAssayData(obj, assay=, layer=, new.data=). Both dispatch on Assay and Assay5.
  • The two accessors disagree on split layers. GetAssayData() is formally superseded by LayerData(), but that matters less than the disagreement. GetAssayData() aborts (“doesn’t work for multiple layers in v5 assay”); LayerData() only warns and returns the first matching layer, silently dropping every other sample. save_counts() is the one function using LayerData(), and only because it calls JoinLayers() first. Without that guard, GetAssayData()’s hard error is the safer default.
  • merge() leaves layers split (counts.1, counts.2, …). Any merge must be followed by SeuratObject::JoinLayers(), which merge_seurat_objects() already does.
  • DimReduc keys are validated against ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*_$. Build reductions with CreateDimReducObject() (which repairs the key) rather than new("DimReduc", ...).
  • Clearing variable features is not possible via VariableFeatures<-. Assay5 stores them as vf_* columns in the assay meta.data, and assigning character()/NULL is a silent no-op. Use DietSeurat(obj, layers = c("counts", "data"), dimreducs = NULL, graphs = NULL) instead — variable features are then left to be overwritten by normalize_counts().

Commands

# load for interactive work
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all(".")'

# full test suite
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'

# a single test file
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all("."); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-import.R")'

# regenerate NAMESPACE + man/ after changing roxygen comments
Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'

# format (config in air.toml) — run on the whole package, not just the files you touched; it's fast
air format .

# full check
R CMD build . && R CMD check scooter_*.tar.gz

NAMESPACE and everything in man/ are generated — never edit them by hand.

Use usethis helpers for package scaffolding when one fits. For example, use use_package() to add a dependency and use_test() to add a test file.

Never make git commits. Leave all changes in the working tree for review; do not git commit, git rm, or otherwise write to git history. Running the tests, R CMD build/check, and R CMD INSTALL (into whichever R library the environment’s R/Rscript resolves to) is fine and does not need to be asked about.

Always end a response with a summary of what changed: every file edited, created, or deleted, listed by path. If the package was installed, say so and give the install path. If nothing was edited, say that too. Report outcomes (files, install path, test counts). Do not list routine steps such as air format ..

Loose .png, .pdf, and .log files in the repo root are generated output. Delete them without asking. Other file types and tests/testthat/ files do not follow this rule.

Architecture

What the package is for vs. what the CLI is for

Read this before deciding where a function belongs — it settles most “should this move?” questions.

  • The package enhances Seurat. Each verb wraps a Seurat function with the parameters this lab has settled on, plus the extra steps and the plots that belong to that step. The added value is the extra steps and plots — a thin binding that only forwards arguments is not worth having. So plotting and writing a step’s outputs are legitimately package work, not something to push out to the caller.
  • The CLI groups related package functions into a pipeline. inst/extdata/scrna-scooter.R exists to sequence package verbs into create / cluster / integrate / … and to handle argument parsing, the analysis directory, and logging. It should call, not implement.
  • The CLI is also a staging area. New or unfinished functions live there first and move into the package once they have settled. Treat a CLI-local function as provisional by default: the question is when it moves, not whether.

Shadowing is a symptom of a pending move, not a pattern to keep. When a CLI function has the same name as a package export, that means the CLI holds extra behavior the package function should absorb. The fix is to move that behavior into the package function and delete the CLI copy — not to rename the CLI copy around the collision.

The S3 dual-dispatch pattern

This is the core idiom. Each public verb is a generic with two methods: .default runs the actual algorithm on a plain matrix/data frame and knows nothing about Seurat; .Seurat pulls the relevant matrix/embedding/metadata out of the object, calls the generic again (landing in .default), then wraps the result back into the object. merge_metadata() and filter_cells() are clear examples of the split. When adding a function that touches expression data, follow it.

Do not add dispatch Seurat already provides. Check the underlying Seurat function’s methods() before reaching for this pattern. NormalizeData() and SCTransform() already dispatch on a matrix and a Seurat object, so normalize_counts() is not dual-dispatch.

dr.R is the exception worth knowing. The .Seurat methods of run_pca/run_tsne/run_umap call the native Seurat functions rather than recursing into .default. For a Seurat object, Seurat computes the reduction. assay is always passed explicitly, never left NULL, so the reduction never silently depends on DefaultAssay(x) at call time. cluster_seurat_object() and create_seurat_object() take the same stance.

Plotting is not optional and is not a parameter. Every .Seurat method in this package writes its standard output unconditionally, every time, flat into the working directory (no subdirectory). See each function’s own roxygen @return for what it writes. The test suite runs from tests/testthat/, so this output lands there. tests/testthat/teardown.R sweeps up the known filenames after the whole suite.

Conventions

[create_seurat_object()] runs the whole load → filter → normalize → reduce → cluster chain in one call. Prefer it when building an object from scratch; use the individual verbs when you need to intervene between steps.

Style: this package follows the tidyverse style guide, formatted by air format ..

Roxygen prose stays short and non-repetitive. A @param entry states what the parameter is. Explain more only when that is not obvious from the name and type alone. Most @param entries should be describable in one clear sentence — resist adding a second sentence, caveat, or backstory unless a caller actually needs it to call the function correctly (a parameter’s history, or why an old design would have been wrong, is not that). Cut any word or clause that doesn’t add information the reader doesn’t already have. When several params share one reason (e.g. several have no default because each describes how a specific object was built), state it once and let the rest give only their own fact — don’t repeat “same reasoning as X” on every one, and don’t restate what’s already obvious from what was just said (e.g. no “either form works” right after listing the accepted forms).

Naming conventions, applied deliberately — match them when adding functions:

  • read_* reads from disk; initialize_* is the bare constructor (a raw-counts object, not useful on its own); create_* returns the usable object.
  • object in function names, obj in variable names. Functions spell it out (merge_seurat_objects()); locals stay short (seurat_obj, so). The serialized file is seurat_obj.qs2 — a filename, so never rename it with a blanket _obj -> _object substitution or every existing analysis dir is orphaned.
  • Don’t split one operation into two functions just because the input type differs. merge_seurat_objects() takes a list that may mix in-memory Seurat objects and analysis-directory paths, resolving whichever it got itself.
  • split_layers_by_batch() (package) splits the assay layers inside one object for IntegrateLayers(). The CLI’s split_seurat_object() splits a cohort into separate analysis dirs, each with its own seurat_obj.qs2. Different outputs, similar names.

Cross-cutting conventions:

  • Adding a metadata column in initialize_seurat_object() shifts the hardcoded ncol() expectations in test-utils.R.
  • Cell IDs are sample_name:barcode. The prefix is applied at load time and Seurat objects are created with names.delim = ":", so orig.ident recovers the sample. Trailing -1 from Cell Ranger is stripped.
  • log_file = NULL is threaded through nearly every function and passed to write_message(), which messages to console and optionally appends to the log. Keep the parameter. Don’t reintroduce a bare write() to the log. Each CLI step writes its own log file, named for that step (create.log, merge.log, integrate.log, cluster.log, hto.log). identify, plot umap and de write no step log file yet.
  • Colors come from get_color_scheme("clusters"|"samples"), not ad-hoc palettes.
  • Name a single-object first parameter x (Seurat object, matrix, or data frame), as base R S3 methods do. A list of objects, or a function with two objects, keeps descriptive names.
  • Add a parameter only if the function body uses it. Do not add one to match sibling functions.
  • Separator banners use message(), not write_message(). Write each fact to the log with its own write_message() call. Do not join facts into one multi-line glue().
  • Prefer intermediate variables to |> chains in new code. This helps debugging. Do not remove existing pipes without a request.

Sample integration

The integrated reduction is named bare int_reduction ("cca"/"rpca"/"harmony"), not "integrated.<method>". CCAIntegration()/RPCAIntegration()/JointPCAIntegration() all default new.reduction to the identical "integrated.dr", while HarmonyIntegration() defaults to bare "harmony". So there is no consistent Seurat convention to match, and the bare names are unambiguous in this codebase.

Pipeline entry point

The package is normally driven through inst/extdata/scrna-scooter.R, a docopt CLI, not from R. A representative single-sample run:

./scrna-scooter.R create out-$sample_name --sample_name=$sample_name --path=$sample_path \
  --min_genes=500 --mt=15 && \
./scrna-scooter.R cluster out-$sample_name --num_dim=30 --reduction=pca && \
./scrna-scooter.R plot umap out-$sample_name --genes_csv=genes.core.csv &

Each step is a separate process reading and rewriting out-$sample_name/seurat_obj.qs2 (serialized with qs2::qs_save()/qs_read(), not saveRDS), which is why they are &&-chained. identify <dir> --cluster_var=<x> is the usual next step; merge, integrate, de, and hto are optional branches. Everything runs relative to the analysis dir (the script setwd()s into it), but --path and --genes_csv are normalizePath()d beforehand, so relative paths to those are resolved against your shell’s cwd.

create — The step stop()s if the analysis dir already exists; a rerun needs the old dir moved or removed first. cluster / plot / identify instead require it to exist. The tSNE/UMAP computed here are a first-pass preview, separate from the real one cluster --num_dim=<n> computes.

  • add_adt_assay_qc() is the one CLI function create still calls, and it is not just QC. It runs the ADT assay’s CLR normalization — nothing else in the pipeline normalizes ADT at all. Its cell-matching logic is now inert, because add_seurat_assay() already intersected the cells.
  • filter_cells() has no targeted-panel exemption. Set min_genes/min_counts explicitly for your data’s scale, or NULL. The inst/extdata 10x fixture tops out at ~250 genes/cell, so fixture-based filter tests need an explicit low min_genes or min_genes = NULL.

cluster — The CLI’s DR steps call the scooter::run_* verbs, not Seurat::Run* directly. So cluster and integrate UMAP go through uwot::umap2() + euclidean, matching the package. Leiden returns 1-based labels while SLM returns 0-based, so the C01/C02/… relabelling shifts from the observed minimum rather than assuming either; changing algorithm must not break this. The res.X column names are what you later pass as --cluster_var to identify.

identify --cluster_var=<x> — works in a clusters-<var>-clust<n>/ subdirectory (created and setwd()’d into first). calculate_cluster_markers() runs standard wilcox, then pairwise wilcox too if under 20 clusters. It calls plot_cluster_markers_heatmap() and plot_cluster_markers_top() itself, so identify never calls those two directly.

hto — both steps are CLI-local: split_adt_hto_assay() demultiplexes and calls plot_hto_qc() itself; the CLI then keeps only hash.class == "Singlet" cells and hands off to split_seurat_object(), which writes one split-<value>/ subdirectory per library_hash value (skipping any with 10 or fewer cells). Each split gets its own fresh normalize/PCA/tSNE/UMAP pass, because a DietSeurat() earlier stripped scale.data/reductions. split_seurat_object()’s dr_num_dim/dr_num_neighbors params are never reachable from the CLI: the hto call site doesn’t pass them, so dr_num_dim = 0 skips clustering.

plot umap (--genes_csv=<x> | --cluster_var=<x>) — docopt makes the two mutually exclusive. --genes_csv calls the CLI-local plot_dr_umap_genes(). It silently switches DefaultAssay to ADT when the gene list overlaps the ADT assay better than RNA — surprising if a sample has ADT and you meant RNA. --cluster_var calls the package function plot_dr_umap_clusters().

de --cluster_var=<x> --group_var=<x> — shares the identify/de block’s setup and clusters-<var>-clust<n>/ subdirectory. A lone de run without identify still creates and moves into it.

No shadow functions remain in the CLI. merge’s and split_seurat_object()’s sequences call normalize_counts() + run_pca() from scratch before the tSNE/UMAP preview, since the object reaching them has no scale.data/PCA of its own yet. The two blocks are similar glue, left inline rather than wrapped in a function. Revisit only if a third call site needs the same sequence.

Files that are not live code

  • R/functions-unprocessed.R — entirely commented out. Legacy CLI functions kept as a porting backlog. Don’t treat it as an API; mine it only when reimplementing something with no live counterpart yet.
  • R/deprecated.R holds thin wrappers, one per package function actually renamed (not deleted/absorbed). Each wrapper only forwards arguments — no logic lives here, ever; fix the replacement function instead. A function absorbed into another has no single replacement to point a deprecate_warn() at, so it gets no shim.
  • Before adding a shim for a rename, check git status on the file the old name lives in. A shim is only warranted if the old name was ever in a committed version — otherwise there is no possible external caller to protect, and the shim is pure cruft. M (modified, previously committed) means the name was real and needs one; ?? (untracked, never committed) means it didn’t.

Move backlog (CLI staging -> package)

Moving a function means its extra steps and plots become part of the package verb it wraps, and the CLI copy is deleted, not renamed — never rename the CLI copy just to dodge a collision with the package export it should eventually absorb into.

Recurring pattern worth knowing before tackling what’s left: a CLI-only global (like colors_clusters) usually has to become a real parameter first (color_scheme, defaulting to get_color_scheme("clusters")); a moved function’s own dependencies (like pheatmap) may need adding to Imports; and moving a function into the package can activate an existing same-name shadow that was only ever harmless because nothing called it unqualified from inside the package.

Remaining:

  1. add_adt_assay_qc() — ADT-specific CLR normalization with no package home.
  2. split_seurat_object() — the last composite in staging. R/split.R is its natural home.
  3. The rest of the ADT/HTO block — plot_adt_qc(), split_adt_hto_assay(), plot_hto_qc(), the least settled.

Deferred / planned

  • suffix (run_pca()/run_tsne()/run_umap()) never propagates between calls. It always defaults to "", and nothing reads it back off a computed reduction. So the output reduction name is always literally "tsne"/"umap". Calling either twice on one object (e.g. a first-pass preview, then the real one) silently overwrites the previous reduction’s data. The plot filenames avoid this by baking assay/reduction/num_dim/group_by into file =; the object storage has no equivalent. Flagged, not fixed; leave suffix’s blank default alone unless asked.

Non-obvious gotchas

  • The CLI’s create step calls create_seurat_object() directly, not through do.call(), on purpose. A do.call() at the top level of the call stack makes SeuratObject’s LogSeuratCommand() misattribute commands logged inside create_seurat_object() (e.g. FindVariableFeatures()) to the do.call(). The correct FindVariableFeatures.<assay> entry never gets recorded, so normalize_counts()’s later HVFInfo() call fails with “Please run either ‘FindVariableFeatures’ or ‘SCTransform’”. create_seurat_object() accepts a length-zero num_dim and falls back to its own default, so the CLI needs no do.call().
  • plot_dr_group() sleeps one second between writes on purpose. It keeps the modification times of the output files distinct so they sort in the order they were produced. Removing it as an “optimization” silently scrambles that ordering.
  • Don’t build filter_cells()’s second subset() from only the default assay’s features. subset(features =) deletes any assay with no feature in that list, so a bare subset(features = names(detected)) built from rowSums() on the default assay alone silently drops the ADT/HTO assays (their nCount_* metadata columns survive, which is what makes it hard to spot). Carry the non-default assays’ features through, the same guard merge_seurat_objects() already has.
  • The CLI no longer writes counts.*.csv.gz at all. The save_counts() calls in create, merge and integrate are commented out on purpose — the tables are rarely used and are expensive to produce. Run scooter::save_counts() by hand against the saved .qs2 object when one is actually needed. Do not “fix” this by uncommenting them.
  • cluster.R does not shadow Seurat::FindAllMarkers(). The package-wide @import Seurat makes the real one resolve unqualified — don’t reintroduce a local copy.
  • FindClusters.default() names its columns res.<resolution> directly — the seurat_snn_res. prefix only comes from the .Seurat method.
  • run_umap.default() (the matrix path) uses uwot::umap2() and must pin nn_method = "annoy": a direct umap2()’s automatic nearest-neighbor choice is not reproducible under set.seed(), so dropping that argument silently makes every UMAP run produce a different embedding. The .Seurat path calls Seurat::RunUMAP(umap.method = "uwot2"), which stays reproducible via seed.use without the pin (verified on large data).
  • normalize_counts(), cluster_seurat_object(), and integrate_layers() each force future::plan(future::sequential) unconditionally before doing anything else (each function’s own roxygen states the conclusion; the benchmark data behind it lives only here). Benchmarked against real objects (1.7k-224k cells), and the answer differs by function:
    • normalize_counts(): sequential ties or wins at every size tested; multisession is up to 6.5x slower, not faster, and can fail outright somewhere around 100k cells (future.globals.maxSize, or a memory-pressure kill — not a fixed cell-count threshold; it depends on the memory available to the job).
    • calculate_clusters(): multisession can be meaningfully faster on mid-size objects, but it crashed (worker OOM-killed) at 50k cells in this session’s memory allocation. Merged/integrated objects are exactly where the pipeline tends to reach this scale, so unconditional sequential was kept anyway, trading away the speedup for predictability.
    • integrate_layers(): no measured difference either way, up to ~50k cells across 8 batches. The guards live inside each function, not in a shared wrapper, because their call graphs don’t funnel through one. integrate_layers() is a standalone entry point for interactive use. The guards are deliberate even when nothing upstream sets a plan — defense against a caller having its own unrelated multisession plan set. FindNeighbors()’s own nearest-neighbor step was never at risk: it force-sets its own sequential plan internally and restores the caller’s plan on exit.
  • mad_outlier_bounds() runs over all cells on purpose. Debris cells widen the MAD and so loosen the upper bound. The bounds match scater::isOutlier() exactly. Do not add a debris pre-filter. Use --max_genes to remove extreme cells.
  • Per-sample splits use up to 30 dimensions. Merged and pooled analyses use up to 50. Single samples are more uniform. Do not unify the two caps.
